title: DGGI unearths clandestine pan masala and tobacco manufacturing network in Uttar Pradesh; 27 undeclared pouch-packing machines seized, evasion of about ₹185 crore detected
subtitle:
Proprietor arrested and remanded to judicial custody; 15.5 lakh pouches of finished goods seized from six premises in Chitrakoot and Banda
Capacity-based cess and taxation regime came into effect under the Health Security se National Security Cess Act, 2025 (HSNS) applicable on pan masala, and central excise levy imposed on chewing tobacco, jarda and gutkha under the Central Excise Act, 1944, on 1st February 2026 respectively
Since 1st February 2026, DGGI formations have booked 27 cases involving suppression of production, clandestine clearance and evasion of the applicable levy, detecting evasion of duty, tax and cess of ₹668 crore; with 131 pouch-packing machines have been seized; 17 persons arrested
body_text:
The Lucknow Zonal Unit of DGGI has busted a clandestine manufacturing operation for pan masala, scented jarda and gutkha spread across six premises in Chitrakoot and Banda districts of Uttar Pradesh. Acting on specific intelligence developed by the Unit, officers started coordinated searches around midnight on 18.08.2026 at these premises, which are connected with two firms, one engaged in the manufacture of pan masala and allied products and the other in trading.
The searches led to detection of 27 undeclared pouch-packing machines comprising 6 machines for scented jarda , 9 for pan masala and 12 for dohara/desi gutkha . Mixing, areca nut crushing and drying machines were also found. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 15,50,922 pouches of finished goods, comprising pan masala , chewing tobacco, scented jarda and sugandhit supari . Raw material and packing material seized includes 32.9 MT of areca nut and cut areca nut, 2.8 MT of tobacco, 8.4 MT of packing material, pouches and laminates, 470 kg of katha powder, 850 kg of glycerine, 545 kg of essence and 256 kg of unpacked pan masala . Evasion of GST, HSNS Cess and Central Excise duty of approximately ₹185 crore has been detected so far.
Evidence indicates that the operation was run through a network of unregistered premises using undeclared machinery, and the finished goods were cleared clandestinely without payment of applicable GST, HSNS Cess and Central Excise duty. The proprietor of the manufacturing firm was prima facie found to be the person organising and managing the clandestine manufacture and clearance. He was arrested on 19.08.2026 under Section 26 of the HSNS Cess Act, 2025 and Section 13 of the Central Excise Act, 1944, and produced before the Special Chief Judicial Magistrate (Customs), Lucknow, who remanded him to judicial custody. Investigation is continuing and further recoveries are expected.
A capacity-based cess and taxation regime came into effect on 1 st February 2026 in the pan masala and tobacco sector. Under the Health Security se National Security Cess Act, 2025 (HSNS) capacity-based monthly cess is applicable on pan masala , which is computed based on number, type and capacity of packing machines installed. A similar capacity-based central excise levy is imposed on chewing tobacco, jarda and gutkha under the Central Excise Act, 1944. Unscrupulous manufacturers try to avoid these imposts by using undeclared machines clandestinely. To counter this, Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI) has stepped up intelligence-led enforcement in this sector, combining data analytics with coordinated field operations across its formations.
Since 1 st February 2026, DGGI formations across the country have booked 27 cases involving suppression of production, clandestine clearance and evasion of the applicable levy, detecting evasion of duty, tax and cess of ₹668 crore. Voluntary payment of ₹11.7 crore has been made during the course of investigation. A total of 131 pouch-packing machines have been seized and 17 persons arrested.
****
SR/KMN

enrichment.summary: The DGGI's Lucknow Zonal Unit raided six premises in Chitrakoot and Banda districts of Uttar Pradesh, busting a clandestine pan masala, jarda and gutkha manufacturing network. Officers seized 27 undeclared pouch-packing machines, 15.5 lakh pouches of finished goods, and raw materials, detecting tax evasion of about ₹185 crore; the proprietor was arrested and remanded to judicial custody. Since the capacity-based cess/excise regime for this sector began on 1 February 2026, DGGI has booked 27 cases nationwide, detecting ₹668 crore in evasion, seizing 131 machines and arresting 17 persons.
enrichment.context:
India introduced a capacity-based taxation regime for pan masala and tobacco products effective 1 February 2026, replacing or supplementing ad valorem GST with a levy computed on the number, type and capacity of installed pouch-packing machines. This is implemented through the newly enacted Health Security se National Security (HSNS) Cess Act, 2025 for pan masala, and a parallel capacity-based central excise levy under the Central Excise Act, 1944 for chewing tobacco, jarda and gutkha. The rationale behind capacity-based taxation is that it is harder to evade than transaction-based GST, since it is pegged to machine capacity rather than self-reported production and sales, which had previously enabled widespread underreporting in this high-evasion sector.

The DGGI (Directorate General of GST Intelligence) is the premier intelligence and enforcement agency under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), tasked with combating GST and indirect tax evasion. This bust is part of a broader crackdown, with 27 cases and ₹668 crore in evasion detected nationally since the new regime began, indicating both the scale of the problem in the pan masala/gutkha sector and the intensified enforcement using data analytics and coordinated raids to counter undeclared machinery being used to bypass the new capacity-linked cess and excise structure.

prelims_questions.question: The capacity-based cess on pan masala mentioned in recent enforcement actions is levied under which of the following legislations?
options: The Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017
The Health Security se National Security (HSNS) Cess Act, 2025
The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that a capacity-based monthly cess on pan masala is applicable under the Health Security se National Security (HSNS) Cess Act, 2025, computed based on the number, type and capacity of packing machines installed.

prelims_questions.question: Which agency under the CBIC conducted the raids leading to the seizure of undeclared pouch-packing machines in Uttar Pradesh?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release identifies the DGGI's Lucknow Zonal Unit as the agency that conducted the coordinated searches and busted the clandestine manufacturing network.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the rationale behind shifting to a capacity-based taxation regime for sectors like pan masala and tobacco products in India. How effective is such a regime in curbing tax evasion compared to transaction-based GST?

Examine the role of intelligence-led enforcement agencies like the DGGI in strengthening indirect tax compliance in India. What challenges do such agencies face in tackling clandestine manufacturing operations?

study_notes.reason: The release carries a testable factual core (HSNS Cess Act 2025, capacity-based taxation mechanism, DGGI's institutional role) alongside analytical value on why capacity-based taxation is designed to curb evasion in a high-leakage sector.

prelims.point: HSNS (Health Security se National Security) Cess Act, 2025 imposes a capacity-based monthly cess on pan masala, computed from the number, type and capacity of installed pouch-packing machines.
prelims.why_important: A newly enacted, specifically named Act with a distinctive taxation mechanism is a natural target for a fact-based prelims question.

prelims.point: Chewing tobacco, jarda and gutkha are taxed via a capacity-based central excise levy under the Central Excise Act, 1944, distinct from the HSNS Cess applicable to pan masala.
prelims.why_important: UPSC often tests such distinctions between two similarly-worded but legally separate levies applying to related products.

prelims.point: DGGI (Directorate General of GST Intelligence) functions under the Central Board of Indirect Customs and Indirect Taxes (CBIC) as the premier indirect tax intelligence and enforcement agency.
prelims.why_important: Institutional placement of enforcement bodies under their parent ministries/boards is a recurring prelims theme.

prelims.point: The capacity-based regime for pan masala and tobacco came into effect from 1 February 2026, replacing/supplementing the earlier ad valorem GST approach for this sector.
prelims.why_important: Knowing the effective date helps place related current-affairs facts and figures in correct chronology.

mains.point: Capacity-based taxation (pegged to machine numbers/capacity) is harder to evade than transaction-based GST because it does not rely on self-reported production and sales figures.
mains.theme: Indirect tax reform and evasion control
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on how tax design choices can reduce evasion in sectors prone to underreporting, e.g. 'Discuss how the structure of a tax can itself be an anti-evasion tool.'

mains.point: Despite the new capacity-based regime, evasion persists through undeclared/clandestine machinery and unregistered premises, showing that legal design alone cannot fully close enforcement gaps.
mains.analytical_use: Supports 'critically examine' style questions on whether stricter tax structures are sufficient without matching enforcement capacity.

mains.point: DGGI's use of intelligence-led, data-analytics-driven coordinated enforcement across formations nationally indicates a shift toward proactive detection rather than reactive audit-based tax administration.
mains.analytical_use: Can be deployed in answers on technology and data analytics in improving governance and revenue collection.

mains.point: High-value, high-frequency small-transaction sectors like pan masala/gutkha are structurally prone to large-scale tax evasion, given cash-based, fragmented, low-visibility production networks.
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for questions asking why certain sectors are chronically tax-evasion-prone and what structural remedies apply.
